findings.title: The fix put a NEW column read into probeBanState's statement, and that statement is still executed by no test - nulling deleted_at neutralises the new auth_identity_deleted refusal and passes all 47
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Not equivalent: `deleted_at` is the sole input to `state.deleted`, which is the sole gate on the brand-new `auth_identity_deleted` refusal, so the mutant silently removes a refusal arm the runbook now documents to operators. Not a proven-fake test: no test claims the statement - the unit suite mocks `sql` entirely and every live-DB suite short-circuits on the to_regclass guard, because scripts/ci/test-db-bootstrap.sql:53-57 provisions schema auth with auth.uid() and NO auth.users relation. So this is an ORACLE gap (inconclusive), not a P0. Second, sharper half, measured not reasoned: I built a real auth.users in the local test DB inside a rolled-back transaction and dropped the column - probeBanState THROWS `column "deleted_at" does not exist`, and nothing in revokeAdmin or main() catches it, so the script would die with EXIT_FAILED. auth.users.deleted_at is a GoTrue column since 2022 and both projects are modern, so this is a loud failure on an unlikely target rather than a silent one - but it is a new hard dependency on a second auth-schema column that no repo fixture provisions and no test pins.
findings.reason: FIXED by the orchestrator at the round-2 cap. findings.title: The 15s Auth timeout the fix added is pinned by nothing - deleting the whole global.fetch AbortSignal.timeout block passes all 47
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Unexecuted branch, so inconclusive/oracle rather than P0: main() is not exported and no test imports it. `rg AUTH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS scripts/` returns three hits, all inside the production file - the constant is exported and nothing consumes it. The bound is real when it runs: I confirmed against the installed tree that supabase-js 2.106.2 forwards settings.global.fetch into _initSupabaseAuthClient (dist/index.mjs:656, :803, :822), so it does reach auth.admin.updateUserById; that AbortSignal.timeout is constructed per invocation inside the arrow function, so 15s is per-request and not per-client-lifetime; that Node's timeout signal is unref'd, so it cannot hold the CLI open; and that auth-js 2.106.2 never sets its own `signal` (dist/main/lib/fetch.js:117 spreads requestParams only), so the override clobbers nothing. What is missing is any oracle: the spec reviewer's fix can be deleted in a later edit and ship green, and the failure mode it prevents is a CLI that hangs forever mid-revoke.
findings.reason: FIXED by the orchestrator at the round-2 cap. The client options are extracted as the exported, fetch-injectable `authClientOptions()`, with two tests: one asserting an AbortSignal reaches every request and AUTH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS is 15000, one asserting the signal is per-request rather than shared. Mutants re-executed: dropping the AbortSignal.timeout KILLED, hoisting it to one shared signal per client KILLED.

findings.title: Missed sibling case: the horizon fix added a short-ban test for --revoke and none for --restore, so the restore arm of alreadyInTargetState is unpinned against a live ban
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Swapping the restore arm from `!state.bannedNow` to `!state.bannedForFullTerm` passes all 47. Arbiter: the branch IS executed - both restore tests reach it - but neither fixture discriminates, because queuePreflight offers exactly two ban shapes, null and a 100-year ban, and the two predicates agree on both. That makes it plausibly-equivalent-under-the-tested-inputs, i.e. an oracle gap, not a proven-fake test. The behaviour the mutant buys is the exact RT-03 shape in the other direction: a `--restore` over a live ban shorter than 365 days would print `ALREADY ACTIVE: users.id=... is not banned; nothing written.` and exit 0 while the admin is still banned. The shipped predicate is correct; what is missing is the mirror of the case the fix DID add for revoke ('re-applies the revoke over a short pre-existing ban'). One fixture closes it: queue a ban inside REVOKE_HORIZON_MS and assert a restore still calls updateUserById.
